candidates.changed_node: dropped the dollar_volume-normalized CS_RANK branch entirely; changed the surviving open-normalized branch's aggregator from a smoothed level (TS_MEAN) to its own 21-day dispersion (TS_STD)
candidates.rationale: Parent's own grandparents (both still live) show the open-normalized branch alone (5dd286d81a38617b, TS_MEAN(range/open,63)) carries mean_ic 0.0113, ~100% of the parent's 0.0112, while the dollar_volume branch (85803c2daa426146, window 10) carries only 0.0063 (56%) -- so open is the component doing the work, not dollar_volume. Neither branch can be kept verbatim: each is a >=4-node exact subtree of the still-live parent itself (archive_subtree reject), and this run's own prior simplify attempt on this same parent (round 6) found that any same-aggregator window bump on either grandparent's field just restates its price/liquidity level and fails correlation instead, forcing that attempt to fall back to the weaker dollar_volume leg. dollar_volume is ruled out here because its TS_STD/TS_MIN/TS_MAX/TS_RANK/TS_DELTA space is already densely mined in this archive -- one live member even fuses range with TS_STD($dollar_volume,21) via a coefficient-of-variation term -- whereas no archive member in this run applies TS_STD to $open at all. Swapping the surviving open branch's aggregator from a smoothed level (TS_MEAN) to its own 21-day dispersion (TS_STD) is therefore structurally novel while keeping the stronger leg's field; a close analogue, range/(TS_STD($close,21)+eps), scored fitness 6.483 in a separate arm's archive, supporting the construction generally even though that arm's field/wrapper differ. IC retention could not be verified against the real panel in this session, so this is the best-supported choice given the recorded per-leg ICs, not a confirmed one.

candidates.changed_node: removed the epsilon-guarded /( $close + 1e-8) scaling from the technical leg's ratio, leaving the raw gap ($close - $high) inside TS_RANK
candidates.rationale: TS_RANK(($close-$high)/($close+1e-8), 21) already converts the daily ratio into a 21-day self-relative percentile, which is inherently scale-normalizing within that short a window since a stock's own price level barely moves in 21 sessions -- so the /( $close+1e-8) price-scaling is redundant, the same logic this run's own prior simplify attempt used to drop $close's epsilon guard once wrapped in TS_RANK for this parent's sibling. This version keeps $high, unlike the parent's three live RANK(eps)-RANK(X) siblings (cf8910d8f4106571: TS_DELTA($close,3)/$close; 618d10279664fdd6: TS_SUM($return,63); d81c79a5c4e69097: TS_DELTA($dollar_volume,63)), so it preserves the parent's own 'position relative to today's high' idea rather than swapping to an unrelated field, giving it a better shot at the 80% IC-retention bar than a field swap would. Dropping the division reduces depth from 5 to 4 at the same field count (eps, close, high). No archive member combines TS_RANK($close - $high, ...); the nearest Alpha101 shape (alpha053) buries ($high-$close) inside a much larger normalized TS_DELTA construction, not a 4-node match. The shared RANK(eps) leg already coexists with three other live second legs without exceeding rho 0.80 pairwise (per 23746d2508bcf88d's own admit rationale) -- precedent that this leg alone doesn't force a correlation reject, though not proof for this specific pairing. IC retention is unverified against the real panel in this session.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.


TASK: SIMPLIFY. Each expression below was flagged as more complex than it needs
to be. Return a simpler expression that keeps the same idea.

Simpler means strictly fewer distinct fields, fewer free constants, or less
depth. The simplification is accepted only if it also keeps at least
80% of the parent's fit-window |IC|, so do not remove the component
doing the work. Put the parent's id in `parent_ids` and name what you removed in
`changed_node`.
